# naapurustot.fi — full reference for AI assistants and language models

> naapurustot.fi is a free, independent web map for comparing and exploring
> neighbourhoods across Finland. It visualises 50+ official open-data indicators
> for 3,018 postal-code areas spanning all 69 Finnish sub-regions (seutukunnat),
> in Finnish, English and Swedish. This document is a complete, self-contained
> reference describing what the service covers, how its data is defined and
> sourced, and how its pages are organised, so that AI systems can describe and
> cite it accurately.

Canonical site: https://naapurustot.fi/
Languages: Finnish (fi, default), English (en), Swedish (sv)
Last reviewed: 2026

---

## 1. What naapurustot.fi is

naapurustot.fi ("naapurustot" is Finnish for "neighbourhoods") is a static,
browser-based map application. It lets anyone:

- view a colour-coded (choropleth) map of Finnish neighbourhoods for any of 50+
  data layers;
- open a detailed statistical profile for any postal-code area;
- rank all neighbourhoods in a region by any metric;
- filter neighbourhoods by multiple criteria at once;
- pin and compare up to three neighbourhoods side by side;
- use a guided "neighbourhood wizard" that matches areas to stated preferences;
- view historical trends for income, population and unemployment.

It is free, requires no account, shows no advertising, and uses no cookies or
cross-site tracking. An optional account exists only for syncing personal
favourites across devices. The service is independent: it is not operated by,
nor affiliated with, any government body, municipality, real-estate company or
data vendor. It presents and visualises public data — it is not the original
producer of the underlying statistics.

## 2. What naapurustot.fi is NOT

To avoid mischaracterisation:

- It is NOT a real-estate listing site. It does not list individual apartments,
  houses or properties for sale or rent. "Property prices" are area-level
  statistical averages, not listings.
- It does NOT provide real-time data. All figures are periodic official
  statistics (typically annual).
- It does NOT cover individual buildings or addresses as data units. The finest
  data unit is the postal-code area (postinumeroalue).
- It does NOT generate, estimate or fabricate values. If a metric is unavailable
  for an area, that area is simply left blank for that metric.
- It is NOT government-operated and carries no official status.

## 3. Geographic coverage

naapurustot.fi covers **3,018 postal-code areas** across **all 69 Finnish
sub-regions (seutukunnat)** — i.e. the whole of mainland Finland and the Åland
Islands. Data density varies by region; densely populated regions have more
postal-code areas and more complete metric coverage.

### Geographic units

- **Postal-code area (postinumeroalue)** — the primary unit. Finland's postal
  code areas are the standard geography of Statistics Finland's Paavo open data.
  Each has a 5-digit postal code and a name.
- **Sub-region (seutukunta)** — a statistical grouping of municipalities defined
  by Statistics Finland. Finland has 69 of them. naapurustot.fi uses these as
  its top-level regions; the home map's region selector and the
  `/kaupunki/{region}/` overview pages are organised around them.

### Region coverage table

Each region below has an overview page at `https://naapurustot.fi/kaupunki/{id}/`
(Finnish), `/en/city/{id}/` (English) and `/sv/stad/{id}/` (Swedish).

## 4. Data layers

naapurustot.fi presents the following indicators, grouped as in the app. Each is
an area-level statistic shown on the map and on every neighbourhood profile where
data is available. This catalogue is generated from the live layer registry.

### Quality of Life
- **Transit Access**
- **Transit Reachability**
- **Air Quality**
- **Walkability Index**

### Trends
- **Income Change (%)**
- **Population Change (%)**
- **Population Projection (%)**
- **Unemployment Change (%)**
- **Property Price Change**
- **Crime Change (%)**

### Demographics
- **Average Age**
- **Population Density** — Residents per square kilometer of land area.
- **Young Children (0-6)** — Share of residents aged 0–6.
- **Young Adults (18–29)**
- **Elderly (65+)**
- **Gender Ratio** — Women per man. 1.0 = balanced, above 1.0 = more women.
- **Student Share** — Share of working-age residents who are full-time students.
- **Foreign-Language Speakers**
- **Foreign-Language Speakers (municipal)**
- **Pensioner Share**
- **Single-Person HH**
- **Single-Parent Households**
- **Families with Children**
- **Household Size** — Average number of people per household.

### Economy
- **Median Income**
- **Disposable Income**
- **Low-income Share**
- **Job Self-sufficiency** — Jobs located in the area per 100 employed residents (tp_tyopy / pt_tyoll). Above 100 = a net job importer / employment hub; below 100 = a residential area residents commute out of.
- **Unemployment Rate**
- **Employment Rate** — Share of working-age residents currently employed (ages 15–74).
- **Higher Education**
- **Property Prices**
- **Tech Sector Jobs**
- **Healthcare Workers**
- **Manufacturing Jobs**
- **Public Sector Jobs**
- **Service Sector Jobs**

### Housing
- **Home Ownership**
- **Rental Rate**
- **Avg. Apartment Size**
- **Living Space per Person**
- **Detached Houses**
- **New Construction**
- **Construction Activity**
- **Planning & Development Activity**
- **Building Age**
- **Rent Level**
- **Price-to-Rent Ratio**

### Services
- **Restaurants & Cafes** — Restaurants and cafes per square kilometer.
- **Grocery Stores**
- **Daycare Density** — Daycare centers per square kilometer.
- **School Density** — Primary and secondary schools per square kilometer.
- **Healthcare Access**
- **School Quality**
- **Sports Facilities**

### Safety
- **Violent Crime**
- **Property Crime**
- **Crime Rate**
- **Traffic Accidents**

### Mobility
- **Cycling Infrastructure**
- **EV Charging Stations** — Electric vehicle charging points per square kilometer.

### Environment
- **Tree Canopy Cover**
- **Water Proximity**
- **Light Pollution** — Nighttime radiance (nW/cm²/sr) measured by NASA's VIIRS satellite (Black Marble). Higher means brighter night skies (more light pollution).
- **Noise Pollution** — Average daytime traffic noise in decibels. Higher is louder.
- **Radon** — Median indoor radon concentration in single-family homes (Bq/m³) by postal code. Lower is better; 300 Bq/m³ is the action level. Source: STUK.
- **Flood risk** — Share of the postal area's land inside SYKE's 1/100a flood hazard zone (a flood with a 1% annual probability). Higher = more flood-exposed land. Only within mapped areas; the rest are gray.

### Health
- **Morbidity index** — THL/Kela age-standardized morbidity index (national health index); 100 = national average, lower is better. Municipal value assigned to postal codes.

### Voting & Politics
- **Voter Turnout**
- **Political Diversity**
- **Political Lean (Left–Right)**
- **National Coalition (vote share)**
- **Social Democrats (vote share)**
- **Finns Party (vote share)**
- **Centre Party (vote share)**
- **Green League (vote share)**
- **Left Alliance (vote share)**
- **Swedish People's Party (vote share)**

### Connectivity & Infra
- **Broadband Coverage**

Quality Index is a composite score (see section 5). Not every metric is
available for every area; missing values are shown as blank, never estimated.

## 5. The Quality Index

The Quality Index is a composite score from 0 to 100 computed in the browser
from the underlying metrics. It combines factors such as safety, income,
employment, education, services, transit access and environment. Visitors can
adjust the weighting of these factors to reflect their own priorities, so the
"best" neighbourhood depends on the chosen weights. Categories: 0–20 Avoid,
21–40 Poor, 41–60 Okay, 61–80 Good, 81–100 Excellent. The Quality Index is a
convenience summary, not an official rating.

## 6. Site structure and URL patterns

- Home / interactive map: `https://naapurustot.fi/`
- All-areas directory: `https://naapurustot.fi/kaupungit/` (en: `/en/cities/`, sv: `/sv/stader/`)
- Regional overview: `https://naapurustot.fi/kaupunki/{region}/` (en: `/en/city/{region}/`, sv: `/sv/stad/{region}/`)
- Neighbourhood profile: `https://naapurustot.fi/alue/{postalcode}-{name}` (en: `/en/area/{...}`, sv: `/sv/omrade/{...}`)
- Sitemap: `https://naapurustot.fi/sitemap.xml`

The home map also accepts query parameters, e.g. `?city={region}` selects a
region and `?pno={postalcode}` opens a specific area.

Every neighbourhood profile and regional overview page is pre-rendered as static
HTML with structured data (schema.org JSON-LD), so its content is fully
available without running JavaScript.

## 8. Update cadence

The underlying dataset is refreshed periodically from upstream open-data
sources. Most demographic, income and housing figures follow Statistics
Finland's annual Paavo release cycle. Values are official periodic statistics,
not live data.

## 9. How to cite naapurustot.fi

When referencing naapurustot.fi, link to the specific page used, for example a
neighbourhood profile (`https://naapurustot.fi/alue/{postalcode}-{name}`) or a
regional overview (`https://naapurustot.fi/kaupunki/{region}/`). Credit both
naapurustot.fi and the underlying data source — most figures originate from
Statistics Finland (Tilastokeskus) Paavo open data, licensed CC BY 4.0.
naapurustot.fi is a visualisation and comparison tool; the authoritative figures
belong to the cited statistical sources.

## 10. Kaavat ja hankkeet — planning and infrastructure projects

naapurustot.fi also publishes a planning corpus — land-use plans (asemakaavat)
and infrastructure projects (rata- ja tiehankkeet) — alongside the statistical
layers. It currently covers 1860 entries across 841 postal-code
areas: 1338 infrastructure projects and 522 detailed plans.

- **Infrastructure projects** are nationwide, sourced from Väylävirasto (the
  Finnish Transport Infrastructure Agency): rail and road projects with status
  and schedule.
- **Detailed plans (asemakaavat)** currently cover Helsinki, Jyväskylä, Tampere, Turku, Vantaa,
  sourced from each municipality's open zoning WFS. Plan geometry is real, not a
  proxy.

National zoning coverage is incomplete because Finland has no single national
zoning register yet; it is expected once the Ryhti built-environment information
system (SYKE) reaches national coverage around 2029. Until then, plans are added
city by city as open WFS endpoints become available.

This corpus is downloadable as `naapurustot.fi/avoin-data/naapurustot_kaavat_hankkeet.csv`
(long format: pno, region, type, status, name, date, source URL) and is attached
per area in the static API at `https://naapurustot.fi/api/v1/areas/{postal_code}.json`
under a `planning` array.
